Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: Digital authentication is a core function of the DRCPass system. The Tridentity platform uses secure single-sign-on (SSO) and blockchain-based authentication to allow citizens to verify their digital identity for transactions. The system supports biometric authentication for SIM card registration and financial services. The DRCPass digital ID provides verifiable digital credentials for both public and private sector transactions. The April 2025 validation phase launch confirmed blockchain, biometrics, AI, and zero-knowledge proofs for secure authentication.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: Government portal authentication is a core DRCPass use case. The Tridentity/DRCPass system includes single-sign-on (SSO) to allow Congolese citizens to access and conduct transactions with public institutions through one digital login. The DRC 2026-2030 National Digital Plan envisions a digital government platform underpinned by DRCPass. A functional digital government platform was envisaged by Q1 2026. The existing e-government ecosystem (e-GOV, I-IMPOTS tax portal) has limited integration but the DRCPass is intended as its identity backbone.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No evidence of an individual data access/view mechanism in the current DRCPass system. The Digital Code N°23-010 (2023) establishes rights of data subjects including the right to access their data and request rectification, but these rights are tied to the APD which is not yet operational. The DRCPass Tridentity app does provide citizens a digital identity record, but no specific self-service data portal allowing individuals to view all their stored government data was identified.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: KYC enablement is a primary function. Trident is designated as the exclusive e-KYC service provider for the DRC under the PPP agreement. The DRCPass one-click e-KYC process auto-scores risk and enables digital financial inclusion. The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) Instruction No. 15 requires KYC/AML compliance, and national ID cards (voter cards, passports, driver's licenses) are accepted KYC documents. Law N°04/016 (2004, amended 2022) mandates KYC/CDD. The DRC is a FATF member (on grey list since 2022).

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Judicial oversight exists but is not ID-specific. General constitutional rights, civil law remedies, and court access apply to ID-related disputes. The Digital Code provides for judicial notification by the APD in cases of criminal violations of data protection rules. Citizens can seek damages in court for data misuse. There is no dedicated ID tribunal or ID-specific judicial oversight mechanism identified.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Partial integration between civil registration and the national ID system. A June 2023 MOU between CENI, ONIP and INS aimed to transfer biometric voter enrollment data (45M+ records) to ONIP to underpin national ID issuance. However, the APAI-CRVS snapshot stated that DRC did not have a National Identity Management system in place, and the link between civil registration offices and identity management remains weak. Birth registration is required to obtain a national ID, but only ~40% of children under 5 have registered births (UNICEF data). The civil registration system has 979 local offices but no central repository.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Data sharing rules are partially available. The Digital Code N°23-010 (2023) establishes principles for data transmission and transfer, requiring explicit prior consent for most transfers and an authorisation regime for sensitive data (including national ID numbers and biometrics). However, implementing decrees for the APD have not been issued, so the rules are not yet fully enforceable in practice. The DRCPass PPP contract terms have not been made public, raising transparency concerns flagged by the NTU-SBF Centre for African Studies. AML/KYC rules (Law N°04/016, BCC Instruction No. 15) establish financial data sharing requirements.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Digital ID-specific regulation exists. The Digital Code N°23-010 of 13 March 2023 (Ordonnance-Loi) establishes a framework specifically for digital identity, electronic authentication, e-government (Guichet Numerique), and data protection. It creates institutional bodies including ANCE (Autorité Nationale de Certification Électronique) for trust services/digital certifications. The June 2025 PPP agreement with Trident for DRCPass also operates under this framework. Implementation decrees are still pending.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: A data protection act exists. The Digital Code N°23-010 of 13 March 2023 contains comprehensive data protection provisions (Book III) covering personal data definitions (including biometric data, fingerprints, iris scans), rights of data subjects (consent, confidentiality), obligations of controllers, breach notification, and penalties (USD 3,000-70,000). Previously, Law N°20/017 of 25 November 2020 on Telecommunications included initial data protection provisions. Several implementing decrees remain pending.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: A data protection authority exists in law but is not yet fully operational. The Digital Code (Article 262) mandates creation of the APD (Autorité de Protection des Données). As of 2024, no Prime Ministerial decree has been issued to establish it formally. A Ministerial Decree of 17 August 2024 temporarily transferred APD functions to ARPTIC (Autorité de Régulation des Postes, Télécommunications et Technologies de l'Information et de la Communication), which is considered legally irregular by scholars but has not been challenged. Declaration and authorisation regimes for data processing are therefore not yet in practice.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The national ID card (carte d'identité nationale) issued by ONIP has legal proof status in DRC. It is the primary identity document for citizens. The voter card (issued by CENI) has also functioned as a de facto identity document for legal purposes. Under the Family Code (Law N°16/008, 2016) civil registration documents (birth certificates) are legally required for passports, education, and healthcare. The new DRCPass digital ID is designed to complement physical IDs as a verifiable digital credential for transactions. KYC regulations (BCC Instruction No. 15, AML Law) explicitly accept national ID cards as valid identity documents.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: A legal framework exists. Key legislation includes: Law N°20/017 of 25 November 2020 on Telecommunications and ICT (first data protection provisions); Digital Code N°23-010 of 13 March 2023 (comprehensive digital governance, data protection, cybersecurity, e-commerce, digital identity); Family Code Law N°16/008 of 2016 (civil registration); and KYC/AML Law N°04/016 of 2004 and Law N°22/068 of 2022. ONIP operates under the Ministry of Interior. The digital legal framework provides for national digital ID, electronic authentication, and data governance.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: Foreign vendors dominate. The DRCPass system is exclusively managed by Trident Digital Tech (Singapore) under a 20-year PPP agreement, with Trident as the exclusive e-KYC provider. Previous contracts were held by Idemia (France)/Afritech. The ENCORE civil servant registry was supported by World Bank technical teams. Local capacity in identity management is nascent. There is no evidence of substantive in-country technical maintenance capacity.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: Partial Ministry of Finance oversight. The Inspectorate General of Finance (IGF) investigated the $1.2B ONIP/Afritech/IDEMIA biometric ID contract in 2024 and flagged cost irregularities and illegal financing arrangements, leading to its cancellation. The DRCPass project (valued at $97.1M capex) is documented in Ministry of Planning documents. The UC-PPP (Unité de Conseil & de Coordination du Partenariat Public Privé) oversees PPP governance. However, systematic ongoing Ministry of Finance oversight of the ID system itself is not clearly established, and the DRCPass contract terms remain undisclosed.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: Primarily externally funded. The $97.1M DRCPass system is under a PPP where Trident (private, foreign) bears implementation costs; Trident raised only $2.6M as of September 2025 and the financing structure remains unclear. The ENCORE civil servant biometric project was funded by the World Bank ($250M commitment). Previous ID contracts relied on private foreign financing (Afritech's planned $593M contribution was questioned as unsecurable). President Tshisekedi announced $1B in domestic public investment under the 2026-2030 National Digital Development Plan, but this is aspirational. Additional funding expected from the World Bank (IDEA programme) and French Development Agency.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The DRCPass system uses biometric authentication including both fingerprint and facial recognition (biometric-blockchain binding). Trident's Tridentity platform leverages biometrics, AI, and zero-knowledge proofs. Biometric SIM-card registration links biometrics to verified citizen records. The Digital Code (N°23-010, 2023) explicitly includes fingerprints and iris scans in the definition of biometric personal data. The 2018 CENI voter registration enrolled 45+ million voters biometrically using Gemalto technology, providing biometric data underpinning the new national ID.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: DR Congo has a mixed paper and digital database. The civil registration system (Bureau de l'Etat Civil) maintains largely paper-based records with 979 local offices; there is no single nationwide repository. The ENCORE project created the first digital civil servant directory in 2025. The DRCPass/Tridentity system is blockchain-based and fully digital but is new and in phased rollout. Historical ID records from the CENI voter registration (biometric, digital) exist but are not unified with civil registration. The broader national database situation remains a mix.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: No meaningful interoperability exists as of 2025. The ENCORE World Bank civil servants biometric registry (118,000+ cards issued) plans future integration with payroll (SIGRH-Paie) but is not yet linked to the ONIP population ID system. The DRCPass system plans SSO access across government portals but is still in phased rollout. The UN APAI-CRVS snapshot confirmed DRC had no National Identity Management system in place. The civil registration system (Bureau de l'Etat Civil) and ONIP operate with weak linkages; a MOU between CENI, ONIP and INS was signed in June 2023 to transfer voter enrollment data to ONIP but full system interoperability has not been achieved.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: National ID is accepted for banking/financial services but not yet mandatory. BCC Instruction No. 15 and AML Laws (N°04/016, N°22/068) require KYC using valid identity documents including national ID cards, passports, voter cards, and driver's licenses. Over 60% of the population lacks formal ID, complicating banking access. The DRCPass is designed to drive financial inclusion via digital KYC. Financial institutions accept ID documents but alternative documents (voter cards, passports) are also valid, so no single mandatory ID requirement applies.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The national ID card is free of charge (initial issuance). The Bankable Africa August 2025 report explicitly states the new ONIP scheme will provide 'cards free of charge unless lost or renewed.' The Law N°09/001 of 10 January 2009 guarantees every child the right to birth registration free of charge within 90 days. Previously, the ID system had no published pricing; the new planned scheme commits to free initial enrollment.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Enrollment eligibility is age 18 and above. The planned ONIP national ID card scheme targets citizens of voting age (18+) per the national electoral law (Law N°04/028). The Bankable Africa report on the Margins Group project confirms the system targets adult citizen groups (students, military, Congolese abroad). The DRCPass enrollment requires citizens to first register for their national ID (18+) then download the Tridentity app. No evidence of ID issuance to those under 18 in the national ID programme. Note: CENI voter registration allowed 16-17 year-olds in 2016-2017 on an exceptional basis, but this was for voter cards not the national ID.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Enrollment is mandatory for some. The national ID system is mandatory for Congolese citizens (the law requires citizens to have an identity document), but coverage is extremely low due to implementation failures and lack of card issuance since the 1990s. The DRCPass digital layer is not yet mandatory—citizens download the Tridentity app voluntarily. The Bankable Africa report notes that under the new ONIP scheme, cards will be provided free of charge, suggesting a push toward universal mandatory enrollment, but formal mandatory status for all has not been enforced in practice.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: National ID/birth certificate is accepted for healthcare access but not strictly mandatory. Birth certificates and national ID are cited as prerequisites for accessing healthcare services at health facilities per APAI-CRVS. The Tridentity/DRCPass system is planned to support 'eligibility verification for health and education programs.' In practice, many citizens access healthcare without official documentation due to the low coverage of formal ID. The ENCORE biometric system for civil servants aims to include health workers in future phases.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Population coverage is very low, well below 20%. National ID cards were not issued since the 1990s (Zaire era) until a 2022 pilot of approximately 700 cards in Kinshasa. A July 2023 symbolic launch produced limited cards. Over 60% of the DRC population lack formal identification per VOVE ID and AML compliance sources. Birth registration is only ~40% for children under 5. The World Bank's 2024 Sub-Saharan Africa ID access analysis places the DRC among the lowest-access economies (<70% adult ID ownership). The DRCPass is in early phased deployment as of mid-2025 with no coverage statistics yet available for the digital ID specifically.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No formal independent security review of the DRCPass system has been identified. The DRCPass/Tridentity system was launched in phased rollout from June 2025; no independent security audit or privacy impact assessment has been published. The NTU-SBF Centre for African Studies warned that unless contract terms are made public, the project risks controversy. The previous IDEMIA/Afritech contract was investigated by the IGF (Inspectorate General of Finance) for financial irregularities (not a security/privacy review). Trident claims compliance with international data protection standards and use of encryption, but no external security review has been disclosed.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration using biometric-linked national identity is mandatory and a primary DRCPass use case. The DRCPass/Tridentity system explicitly includes biometric-blockchain binding for SIM card registration to eliminate ghost lines and fraud. ARPTC (Autorité de Régulation des Postes, Télécommunications et Technologies de l'Information et de la Communication) oversees telecom subscriber verification requirements. Uqudo confirms SIM registration compliance requirements are enforced by ARPTC. The Law N°20/017 (2020) on Telecommunications establishes the regulatory framework.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: National ID/identity documents are accepted for social services access but not universally mandatory. Birth certificates are required to access education (school enrollment) and some social services. The DRCPass is designed to facilitate 'more efficient distribution of public services, including subsidies, healthcare, and education.' CNSS (National Social Security Fund) registration is linked to employment identity. However, given that over 60% of the population lacks formal ID, mandatory enforcement is not practically achievable currently. No specific legislation mandating ID for all social services was identified.
